title: They told you to stay away from them.
paragraphs: They told you to stay away from them.

Not because you hated them…
But because deep down—you thought you were better.
You never said it out loud.

That quiet, polished pride that hides behind “standards.”
That subtle distance you keep so no one sees you standing too close to “those people.”
But here’s the tension you don’t want to face:

What if your “righteousness”…
Is just refined rejection?

What if the lines you drew in the name of God…
Are the very lines Jesus came to erase?
It exposes something buried deep inside even the most devoted believer:
Pride that wears the mask of obedience.
He was not living in open sin.

He was disciplined.
Devoted.
A man who walked with Jesus.

Because even a man who saw miracles…
Can still carry prejudice.

Even a man who preached Christ…
Can still limit who Christ is for.

Heavy.
Alive.
Moving with creatures Peter had been trained his entire life to reject.
Out of a belief system so ingrained that even God’s voice sounded wrong to him.
Some of you are there right now.

God is trying to expand your heart…
And you keep resisting because it doesn’t match your categories.
But heaven responds with a sentence that still shakes the Church today:

“What God has made clean, do not call common.”
— Acts 10:15
Because sometimes one confrontation is not enough to break years of pride.
The ones Peter would never invite in.
The ones he would preach around—but not sit beside.

While Peter was still trying to process the vision…
God was already preparing a man named Cornelius.
Everything Peter had been taught to avoid.
And here is where it gets uncomfortable.
God was working in Cornelius’ house…
God is moving in people you have already dismissed.
God is drawing those you have already labeled.
God is healing those you would have kept at a distance.
And when Peter walked into that house…

His upbringing.
His theology.
His prejudice.
His pride.
“Truly I understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears Him and does what is right is acceptable to Him.”
And the cross was never exclusive.
Because this is not just about “them.”
You were never “clean” to begin with.
Sin doesn’t just stain certain people.
You may not have eaten what was forbidden…
But you have thought what was forbidden.
Held onto what God told you to release.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
So here is the uncomfortable truth:
The same grace that reached them…
Is the same grace that had to reach you.
Let that break something in you.
Because pride dies when you remember:
But here is where everything shifts.
Jesus did not come to reinforce your categories.
He came to destroy the walls.
“For He Himself is our peace, who has made both one and has broken down in His flesh the dividing wall of hostility.”
All brought to the same place:
This is where many stop short.
But the Gospel is not vague kindness.
Because Jesus does not just accept you as you are—
He transforms you into who you were created to be.
And some of you need that same repentance today.
Not for what you did publicly…
But for what you believed privately.
Because pride will keep you from people…
Some of you have not rejected others…
And God is saying the same thing to you:
“What I have made clean… do not call common.”
You are not what you were.
But because Jesus paid for it.
His blood speaks louder than your past.
His cross reaches further than your failure.
His grace is deeper than your shame.
So stop standing at a distance.
Because the same God who corrected Peter…
Who are you still calling unclean?
Because grace does not negotiate with pride.
And the Gospel does not just save individuals.
If God is exposing something in your heart…

“Lord, break my pride.
Cleanse my heart.
Teach me to see people the way You do.”
And if something inside you is waking up right now…
